specification.problem: Generate an orthonormal basis of n=3 qubit Bell-like states, each a 2^m-term superposition with amplitudes ±2^{-m/2}, by applying Hadamards on m qubits followed by a multi-qubit controlled-X (CNOT fan-out) layer, with an optional multi-controlled-X (Toffoli-type) variant. Input basis index x selects the basis state.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Single instance n=3, m=2 (m=1 also valid). Variant A: H on 2 controls then CNOT fan-out onto 1 target with f(c)=c1 xor c2. Variant B: H on 2 controls then a doubly-controlled X (CCX) on the target, a nonlinear f(c)=c1 AND c2. Both are generic family members, not the paper's exact two controlled-unitary gates. Qudit extension and entanglement/monogamy analysis are out of scope. Input loading by X gates is an optional parameter x in the build, and the unitary alone has columns |B_x>.

symbols.meaning: number of Hadamard control qubits; states have 2^m terms
input basis label; a in {0,1}^m sets signs, y in {0,1}^{n-m} sets target offset
map {0,1}^m -> {0,1}^{n-m}; linear XOR (variant A) or AND (variant B)
circuit unitary, controlled-X layer times H on controls

equations.label: Bell-like state
equations.description: Output on input |a>|y>; a 2^m-term superposition with amplitudes ±2^{-m/2}.
equations.abstract_quote: The Bell-like states in any basis is superposition of $2^{m}$-terms with equal probabilities (that is, their amplitudes being $\pm 1/\sqrt{2^{m}}$).
equations.justification: Equal-magnitude amplitudes are stated in the abstract; the H plus controlled-X realization is an assumed construction.
assumptions: controls are the first m qubits
f is a Boolean function applied as X^{f(c)} on targets

equations.label: Circuit unitary
equations.description: H on controls then controlled-X on targets. Variant A: CNOT c1->t, CNOT c2->t. Variant B: CCX(c1,c2->t).
equations.justification: Proposed concrete controlled-unitaries; the paper's two gates are not given in the abstract.

equations.label: Orthonormality
equations.description: Outputs form an orthonormal basis because W is unitary.
equations.justification: A unitary maps an orthonormal basis to an orthonormal basis.

equations.label: Instance maps
equations.description: Variant A gives a linear map (CNOT fan-out); variant B gives a nonlinear map (CCX). The two bases differ, so they can have different entanglement content offline.
equations.justification: Smallest concrete choices; B illustrates a multi-controlled gate.

equations.label: Multi-controlled-X
equations.latex: C^{m}X=I-P_1\cdots P_m\otimes I+P_1\cdots P_m\otimes X,\quad P_k=|1\rangle\langle1|_k
equations.description: Standard multi-controlled-X: X on the target only if all controls are |1>. Used in variant B with m=2.
equations.justification: Standard definition. The specialist's predicted eq. (1) and (2) were rejected as not usable here (the first is malformed, the second concerns an unknown gate).

registers.name: c
registers.role: control qubits receiving H, the first qubits in the label

specification.initial_state: Computational basis state |a>|y> loaded by X gates for index x=(a,y). The label is written c1 c2 t with c1 leftmost; in Qiskit little-endian this means qubit 0=c1, qubit 1=c2, qubit 2=t, and the integer index is x=a1+2a2+4y. With no x given, the unitary W is built and column x is |B_x>.

steps.description: Optionally load basis input |a>|y> with X gates.
Apply H to the m control qubits.
Apply the controlled-X layer: CNOT fan-out (variant A) or CCX (variant B), per f.
The output is |B_x>; orthonormality over all x can be checked with the Gram matrix of the columns of W.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Decoding: apply W^dagger and read the computational basis to recover x. Entanglement comparisons (concurrence, negativity, monogamy score) are offline and not implemented.
assumptions: only X-type controlled gates; phase-type gates not implemented
qubit 0 is the least significant bit of the integer index
missing_information: The paper's two specific multiple-qubit controlled-unitary gates
Proof that earlier algorithms are special cases
